standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a connected subset through the absence of a nontrivial relatively open and closed subset, and the continuity of the map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on connected components, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis on the subset and the conclusion about its image.

core_obligations: Pull back a separation: given a subset of the image that is open and closed in the image, the proof pulls it back along the map, where it is again open and closed, this time in the connected subset (proof lines 863-865).

Use connectedness: the preimage is therefore empty or the whole subset, and the proof records that every subset of the image is the image of its preimage under a surjection onto the image (proof lines 865-868).
Conclusion: the pulled-back set being trivial forces the original subset of the image to be trivial, so the image is connected (proof lines 868-871).
proof_roadmap: 取像中既开又闭的子集 A，沿连续映射拉回，得 E 中既开又闭的子集 f^{-1}(A)。
由 E 连通得 f^{-1}(A) 为空或为 E；又 A = f(f^{-1}(A))（把 f 限制到像上是满射），故 A 平凡，于是 f(E) 连通。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the preservation of connectedness under continuous images (author lemma at source lines 855-860, label lemma-image-connected-space). The proof (source lines 862-872) is a complete verification by pulling back: a relatively open and closed subset of the image pulls back to one of the connected subset, connectedness makes it trivial, and the identity expressing a subset of the image as the image of its preimage transfers triviality back (proof lines 863-868). The lemma is the companion of the results on connected components and is used for the connectedness statements later in the chapter. H2.
